# System Designer

> A free browser game for learning and practising system design, with 82 problems, 41 lessons and a simulated traffic day.

For backend engineers, students and interview candidates. Clarify requirements, estimate scale, draw a system and test spikes, outages and retries. Compare reliability, speed, data safety and monthly cost. Playing on systemdesigner.io needs a free Google or GitHub account, and the problems, lessons and guides can be read without one. The code is open source (MIT) and runs with no account. Figures are teaching approximations. Traffic measurements and protocol correctness checks are distinct.

## Start here

- [Home](https://systemdesigner.io/): What the game is and common questions.
- [Problems](https://systemdesigner.io/problems/): Every scenario grouped by industry and difficulty.
- [Lessons](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/): Every lesson in track order.
- [Guides](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/): Practice advice, a day-by-day plan and classic walkthroughs.

## Guides

- [Build the system. Survive the day. See why it held.](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/introducing-system-designer/): Meet System Designer: a free browser game with 82 system design problems, 41 lessons and a traffic day that puts your decisions to work.
- [How to practise system design](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/how-to-practise-system-design/): A practical loop for turning a diagram into a design you can explain: clarify, estimate, predict a failure, test it and revise one decision.
- [A two-week system design interview plan](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/two-week-system-design-plan/): Fourteen days of lessons, traffic experiments and design explanations, with Interview mode in the second week. Every task links to a real lesson or problem.
- [URL shortener walkthrough](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/url-shortener-walkthrough/): Separate durable link storage from fast redirects, estimate the read path and test what happens when a popular link outgrows its cache.
- [Rate limiter walkthrough](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/rate-limiter-service-walkthrough/): Build fair admission for a public API: estimate counters, choose a sharing policy and explain what happens when the limiter cannot answer.
- [Chat system walkthrough](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/chat-app-walkthrough/): Design message identity, durable acknowledgement and reconnect behavior before treating chat as a socket-count problem.
- [News feed walkthrough](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/social-feed-walkthrough/): Estimate fanout work, keep posts authoritative and choose where to assemble feeds for ordinary accounts and celebrities.
- [Notification service walkthrough](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/notification-service-walkthrough/): Separate acceptance from sending, respect provider quotas and reason about expiry and unknown outcomes before claiming delivery once.
- [Caching, load balancing and queues, explained by breaking things](https://systemdesigner.io/guides/caching-load-balancing-queues/): Three small experiments show what caching, load balancing and queues protect, what they cost and how each can fail.

## Problems

- [URL shortener](https://systemdesigner.io/p/url-shortener/): Easy. People paste a long web address and get back a short one. Millions of other people then tap that short link, so reading is almost everything. Keep every tap fast, and never lose a link.
- [Rate limiter for a public API](https://systemdesigner.io/p/rate-limiter-service/): Medium. Developers call your public API from scripts and apps. A few misbehaving or malicious clients can crowd out everyone else. Build limits that are fair, fast and cheap, and that survive a retry storm.
- [Search autocomplete](https://systemdesigner.io/p/search-autocomplete/): Medium. As people type, they expect suggestions after every letter, in the blink of an eye. Most people type the same popular beginnings. When news breaks, one phrase suddenly dominates.
- [Notification service](https://systemdesigner.io/p/notification-service/): Medium. Every other team asks you to send messages: order shipped, new login, a sale starting. You send them by push, email and text through outside providers who have their own limits. Send each message once, and never block the team that asked.
- [Login and single sign-on](https://systemdesigner.io/p/login-sso/): Medium. Employees and customers sign in to many apps through one account. Most of the day is quiet, then 9 am arrives and everyone signs in at once. Attackers also hammer the login with stolen passwords. Let real people in quickly and keep the rest out.
- [Scheduled job service](https://systemdesigner.io/p/job-scheduler/): Hard. Customers register jobs: "call my web address every night at 02:00" or "every hour on the hour". Aim to fire within 5 seconds; work still waiting after 60 seconds counts as failed. Retry safely after a crash. One external effect requires the customer endpoint to honor a stable job occurrence key. Half the world picks the top of the hour, so a huge crowd of jobs comes due in the same second.
- [Object storage service](https://systemdesigner.io/p/object-storage/): Hard. Customers store billions of files, from tiny pictures to huge videos, and fetch them by name. The service must never lose a file, scale without a limit and stay cheap. Most files are written once and rarely read again.
- [Photo sharing](https://systemdesigner.io/p/photo-sharing/): Easy. You are building a photo app. People post pictures and everyone else scrolls through them. Almost all the traffic is people looking at photos, and the photos take up far more room than anything else you store.
- [Podcast hosting](https://systemdesigner.io/p/podcast-hosting/): Easy. You host shows for creators. Listeners press play and download big audio files, and creators upload a new episode now and then. The audio is the bill: every episode downloaded costs bandwidth.
- [News site](https://systemdesigner.io/p/news-site/): Easy. You run a news site. Millions read the same few stories, and when something big happens almost everyone opens the same page in the same minute. Editors publish all day, and readers expect fresh headlines.
- [Music streaming](https://systemdesigner.io/p/music-streaming/): Medium. People search for songs, build playlists and press play. The audio is the heavy part, and a hit song is played by millions at once. Playback must not stutter, even when part of your system fails.
- [Video streaming](https://systemdesigner.io/p/video-on-demand/): Medium. You run a movie and series service for a growing audience. Each viewer pulls a few seconds of video at a time for two hours straight. Bandwidth is the largest cost by far, and everyone wants to start watching in the evening.
- [Short-video feed](https://systemdesigner.io/p/short-video-feed/): Medium. People swipe through an endless feed of clips of 10 to 30 seconds. The next clip must already be on the phone before the swipe. One clip can suddenly get millions of views, and every view is a signal that picks what to show next.
- [Video upload pipeline](https://systemdesigner.io/p/video-upload-pipeline/): Hard. Creators upload videos that must be converted into several qualities before anyone can watch. Conversion is slow, costs real money per video, and the converter sometimes fails on a broken file. Nothing a creator uploads can be lost.
- [Live streaming](https://systemdesigner.io/p/live-streaming/): Hard. Streamers broadcast live and thousands watch together, with a chat on the side. Everyone wants the same piece of video at the same second, so nothing can be saved for later. When a big streamer goes live, the whole audience arrives at once.
- [Comments and likes](https://systemdesigner.io/p/comments-and-likes/): Easy. Under every post sits a like counter and a comment list. Millions tap the heart on the same famous post at the same moment. Showing the exact number is not essential, but showing the person their own like is.
- [One-to-one chat](https://systemdesigner.io/p/chat-app/): Medium. People send short messages to each other from their phones. A message must arrive once, in order, even when the phone is on a bad connection and sends it again. If the other person is offline, the message waits and a notification goes out.
- [Disappearing stories](https://systemdesigner.io/p/stories/): Medium. People post photos and short clips that vanish after 24 hours. Followers tap through a tray of stories every day, and the poster sees who looked. Deleting on time matters: storage must not grow forever.
- [Social feed](https://systemdesigner.io/p/social-feed/): Hard. Every person opens the app and sees a feed of posts from the people they follow. Most people have a few hundred followers, but a few have millions, and when they post, millions of feeds must change. The feed must be fast and your own post must show up at once.
- [Group chat and presence](https://systemdesigner.io/p/group-chat-presence/): Hard. Teams talk in channels with many people. Everyone sees messages in the same order, sees who is online and who is typing, and gets notified when mentioned. At nine every morning thousands of workplaces start at once, and one announcement can reach a channel of tens of thousands.
- [Invoicing and billing](https://systemdesigner.io/p/invoicing-billing/): Easy. Small businesses create invoices, email them to customers and take card payments online. On the last working day of the month everyone sends and chases invoices at once. Nobody may get the same invoice email twice, and no invoice may vanish.
- [Payroll run](https://systemdesigner.io/p/payroll-run/): Easy. On pay day your system tells the payment rail to move salaries for two million employees, then publishes a payslip for each one. Employees open the app at breakfast to see if they were paid. Paying anyone twice is the one thing you must never do.
- [Checkout payments](https://systemdesigner.io/p/payments-checkout/): Medium. Online shops send you their customers at the moment they pay. You call a card processor, record the order and answer in a couple of seconds. When the processor is slow or down, shoppers refresh and tap Pay again.
- [Peer-to-peer wallet](https://systemdesigner.io/p/digital-wallet/): Medium. People split dinner by sending each other money from their phones. A transfer takes money from one balance and adds it to another, and the sender must see the new balance right away. A flaky mobile connection often makes the app send the same transfer twice.
- [Insurance claims](https://systemdesigner.io/p/insurance-claims/): Medium. After a hailstorm, thousands of drivers file claims online, each with a handful of photos. The storm offer ends at 5 pm, so everyone files at the last minute. Every claim must be saved safely, and every customer gets a confirmation email.
- [Buy now, pay later](https://systemdesigner.io/p/bnpl-credit/): Medium. At checkout a shopper picks "pay in four". You score the shopper in a few seconds, then charge the first quarter on their card. The card network sometimes asks you to slow down, and when apps retry, the retries make it worse.
- [Bank ledger](https://systemdesigner.io/p/bank-ledger/): Hard. You run the system of record for a regional bank: every deposit, withdrawal and card settlement is a posting that must be exact and permanent. Customers in two continents read balances all day, and regulators can ask for proof at any time. A bad day for you is a loss of even one posting.
- [Stock order matching](https://systemdesigner.io/p/stock-order-matching/): Hard. Brokers and traders send buy and sell orders, and you pair them fairly: the earliest order at the best price goes first. At the market open a rush of orders arrives in seconds. Every accepted order must be in one agreed sequence, and no trade may be lost or invented.
- [Real-time fraud detection](https://systemdesigner.io/p/fraud-detection/): Hard. Every card payment asks your system "is this fraud?" and wants the answer within about 150 milliseconds. Each check looks up the cardholder's recent habits and runs a model. The holiday shopping rush doubles the volume, and a bad model update can start declining honest customers.
- [Crypto exchange](https://systemdesigner.io/p/crypto-exchange/): Hard. People trade coins, check prices and withdraw funds around the clock from every continent. A sudden price crash makes everyone log in and trade at once, attackers flood you hoping to knock the site over, and a leaked key could empty a wallet. Balances must never be wrong.
- [Clinic appointment booking](https://systemdesigner.io/p/appointment-booking/): Easy. A group of 60 clinics lets patients find a free slot, book it and get a text reminder. Slots open at 8 am, and the phone lines used to melt. Two people must never get the same slot, and reminders must go out even when the text-message company has a bad hour.
- [Lab results portal](https://systemdesigner.io/p/lab-results/): Easy. Labs send results to a portal, patients get a notice that a result is ready and open it. When the notice goes to thousands of people at the same minute, they all open the portal at once. Nobody should get the same notice twice.
- [Patient health records](https://systemdesigner.io/p/health-records/): Medium. A hospital network keeps patient charts, orders, notes and scanned documents for 40 hospitals. Doctors need a chart in under a second, no saved note may be lost when a server or a building fails (in a whole-region disaster, at most the last minute of edits may need re-entering from the ward), and an auditor can walk in any day and ask you to prove who looked at what.
- [Telehealth video visits](https://systemdesigner.io/p/telehealth-video/): Medium. Patients join a video visit with a doctor from their phone. Most calls go straight between the two people, but the platform runs the waiting room, chat, sign-in, the join link and a relay for the calls that cannot connect directly. A bad minute here means a patient staring at a spinner.
- [Pharmacy stock and refills](https://systemdesigner.io/p/pharmacy-stock/): Medium. A pharmacy chain with 4,000 stores tracks how many boxes of each medicine every store has, takes refill requests, and shows patients which nearby store has their medicine today. If the system says a store has a box that is gone, a patient makes a wasted trip.
- [Vaccine sign-up surge](https://systemdesigner.io/p/vaccine-signup-surge/): Hard. A county opens 80,000 vaccine appointments at 8 am. Within seconds, thousands of people reload and bots try to grab slots. The site must stay up, never sell the same slot twice, and be fair to people on a phone with a poor signal.
- [Health readings from a wearable](https://systemdesigner.io/p/wearable-health/): Hard. A wearable records health readings even when its phone or cloud service is unavailable. Keep raw readings on the device when possible and upload only consented summaries in sparse batches. The system must not lose locally saved readings during a supported outage, and deleting an account must have a verifiable end-to-end workflow.
- [Benefits application portal](https://systemdesigner.io/p/benefits-portal/): Easy. People apply for food, health or housing help on a state site. Forms are long, people save drafts and upload documents, and a caseworker team reviews each one. The last week of the month is busy, and an auditor checks the privacy and access controls once a year.
- [Course enrollment day](https://systemdesigner.io/p/course-enrollment-day/): Medium. Registration opens at 9 am for 40,000 students, and a handful of popular courses have only 30 seats each. Everyone clicks "enroll" at the same moment, and when the page is slow they click again. A seat must go to exactly one student.
- [Online exam](https://systemdesigner.io/p/online-exam/): Medium. A national board runs a two-hour online exam for 200,000 students in three regions at the same time. Answers save automatically every half minute, a live heartbeat shows the student is still there, and proctoring marks suspicious events. Every saved answer matters. A minute of outage at the wrong time is a national story.
- [Tax filing deadline](https://systemdesigner.io/p/tax-deadline-surge/): Hard. A national tax site lets 30 million people file online. Most wait until deadline day, and traffic climbs all evening to a final-hour rush. People upload forms, check what they owe and pay. A mistake in a payment or a leak of tax data is a national story.
- [Package tracking](https://systemdesigner.io/p/package-tracking/): Easy. You run the tracking page for a parcel company. People refresh it again and again while they wait for a delivery, and depots send a scan every time a parcel moves. Keep the page fast, lose at most the last minute of scans in a failure (scanners keep a copy and can resend), and make sure a broken text-message service cannot slow anything down.
- [Fleet telemetry](https://systemdesigner.io/p/fleet-telemetry/): Medium. A freight company has 150,000 trucks that each send a batch of sensor readings every 30 seconds. Dispatchers watch live maps and analysts run reports. You must take in every batch, keep a month of detail cheaply, and survive the moments when thousands of trucks come back online at once.
- [Food delivery](https://systemdesigner.io/p/food-delivery/): Medium. You run food delivery in a few big cities. People browse menus, pay for an order, and watch a courier move on a map. Dinner time is brutal, and the payment company sometimes slows down. Nobody may be charged twice, and no paid order may vanish.
- [Ride-hailing dispatch](https://systemdesigner.io/p/ride-hailing-dispatch/): Hard. You run dispatch for a big metro area. About 100,000 drivers send a position every 4 seconds, and riders ask for cars near them. When a stadium empties, thousands of riders ask for a car from the same few blocks at the same moment. Match riders to drivers fast, and never charge a trip twice.
- [Maps and routing](https://systemdesigner.io/p/maps-routing/): Hard. You run a maps app with places, routes and live traffic. Map pictures never change much, but route lookups, place search and traffic from moving phones do. Soon a whole new continent will start using it. Keep maps fast everywhere without paying to serve the same picture twice.
- [Restaurant reservations](https://systemdesigner.io/p/restaurant-reservations/): Easy. Diners look up restaurants, check which tables are free tonight and book one. Looking is easy to speed up. Booking is not: two people must never get the same table. Friday at 5 pm is the busy moment.
- [Hotel booking](https://systemdesigner.io/p/hotel-booking/): Medium. You run a hotel booking site. People search for rooms, open hotel pages and book. Search can be a little behind, but you must never sell the last room twice. Bots copy your prices all day, and sometimes the payment company slows down.
- [Airline booking](https://systemdesigner.io/p/airline-booking/): Hard. You run the booking system for an airline. Fare searches are heavy, seats are limited, and every flight needs the right number of tickets, no more and no fewer. You depend on a partner system for fares from other airlines, and it has strict limits. A fare sale and a slow partner will both happen on the same day.
- [Concert ticket drop](https://systemdesigner.io/p/concert-ticket-drop/): Hard. Tickets for a huge tour go on sale at 10:00 sharp. Hundreds of thousands of fans arrive in the same minute, bots arrive earlier, and everyone refreshes when the page stalls. There are 40,000 seats. Sell each one once, charge each buyer once, and keep the site standing.
- [EV charging network](https://systemdesigner.io/p/ev-charging-network/): Easy. Thousands of chargers report their status every few seconds and send a record when a session ends. Drivers open an app to find a free charger. A session record must never be lost or counted twice, because it becomes a bill.
- [Smart home](https://systemdesigner.io/p/smart-home-hub/): Medium. One million homes have a hub that keeps a live connection to your cloud. The hub reports its devices every few minutes, and the phone app sends commands like "lock the door". Commands must feel instant and must not be repeated. Once in a while a power cut ends and every hub reconnects together.
- [Smart power grid](https://systemdesigner.io/p/smart-power-grid/): Medium. A power company has 5 million smart meters. Each reports usage every 15 minutes, and they all try on the quarter hour. Customers see their usage, billing needs exact totals for seven years, and a regulator checks that records are kept safely. Control commands to home batteries and thermostats must never run twice.
- [Factory sensors](https://systemdesigner.io/p/industrial-sensors/): Medium. A factory has thousands of machines, each sending readings many times a second. Engineers open charts of the last hour and last month, and an alarm must fire within seconds when a reading goes out of range. The data grows without end.
- [Firmware rollout](https://systemdesigner.io/p/firmware-rollout/): Hard. A new firmware goes out to a million smart devices at 03:00 when they are idle. Every device asks "is there an update?", then downloads the same file in pieces, then reports back. If they all wake together, they can flatten your service, and a device that fails to update must not be left broken.
- [Semantic search](https://systemdesigner.io/p/semantic-search/): Easy. A help center lets people type a question in plain words and finds the right articles even when the words differ. Each question is turned into a list of numbers (a vector) and matched to similar articles. Many people ask the same few questions.
- [Recommendations](https://systemdesigner.io/p/recommendations/): Medium. Every page shows a row of things the visitor might like. A ranking model builds each row, but the model is slow and costly. The row must appear instantly, even when the model is having a bad day.
- [Ad serving](https://systemdesigner.io/p/ad-serving/): Hard. Each page view asks you to pick the best ad in about a quarter of a second: check who is allowed to see what, score the candidates with a model, run a quick auction and answer. Every impression and click must be counted exactly because money depends on it.
- [AI chatbot serving](https://systemdesigner.io/p/ai-chatbot-serving/): Hard. Millions of people ask your assistant questions. Each reply takes a GPU several seconds, and GPUs are expensive and sometimes simply unavailable. Keep replies flowing, protect your wallet from abuse, and have a plan for when the GPUs run out.
- [Leaderboards](https://systemdesigner.io/p/leaderboards/): Easy. Players send their score at the end of every match and open the top-100 table all day. Everyone looks at the same top 100, which makes that one answer extremely popular. A tournament final will make it much worse.
- [Multiplayer matchmaking](https://systemdesigner.io/p/matchmaking/): Medium. Players press Play and wait. You must put them in a match with others nearby, with similar skill, in a few seconds. Players in a far-away region will have a bad time, so you must keep each region close.
- [Patch day downloads](https://systemdesigner.io/p/game-patch-day/): Medium. A popular game ships a 5 GB update at 10 am. Millions of players press Update within the same hour. The files are identical for everyone, so the work is moving huge amounts of data without a huge bill, while players still log in and play.
- [Battle royale launch](https://systemdesigner.io/p/battle-royale/): Hard. On launch night millions of players queue for matches of 100. Each match streams positions many times a second, the lobby shows the live player count, and one patch notes page is opened by everyone. Connections must stay open, a match server dying must preserve acknowledged progress within the stated recovery point, and a few hot items, like the daily reward, are hit by everybody.
- [Calendar and invites](https://systemdesigner.io/p/calendar-invites/): Easy. People view their week, create meetings and invite others. Each invite sends an email or phone alert. Monday at 9 am everyone opens the calendar at once. A repeated send must never produce two invites, and a slow email partner must not slow the calendar.
- [File sync](https://systemdesigner.io/p/file-sync/): Medium. A folder on your laptop mirrors to the cloud and to your other devices. Small changes must arrive quickly, big files must upload reliably, and a shared folder with thousands of people must not melt the metadata service.
- [Collaborative documents](https://systemdesigner.io/p/collaborative-docs/): Hard. Many people edit the same document at the same moment and everyone must see a consistent result in a fraction of a second. Edits must never be lost, even if a server crashes in the middle of typing or two people type in the same place.
- [Email service](https://systemdesigner.io/p/email-service/): Hard. Mail arrives from the whole internet, including a lot of spam, and must land in the right inbox. People open, search, send and attach. Never lose a message, and keep search fast even over years of mail.
- [Notes that sync across your devices](https://systemdesigner.io/p/device-notes/): Hard. Build a notebook that works on a phone and laptop, including a month offline. Edits should reach connected foreground devices in under a second, concurrent work must not disappear, and the server should not need plaintext notes. Push wakes devices; durable sync must work when push does not.
- [Shopping cart](https://systemdesigner.io/p/shopping-cart/): Easy. Shoppers browse products, drop things in a cart and come back later from another phone. Browsing is most of the traffic and can be a little old. The cart itself must always show what the shopper just added.
- [Flash sale inventory](https://systemdesigner.io/p/flash-sale-inventory/): Medium. At noon a hot item goes on sale with only a few thousand units. A huge crowd arrives in the same minute and everyone taps Buy. Stock must never go below zero, nobody should be charged for an item that is gone, and the site must not fall over.
- [Black Friday marketplace](https://systemdesigner.io/p/black-friday-marketplace/): Hard. Once a year a marketplace puts thousands of deals live at the same minute. Millions browse and search, a few doorbuster items get hammered, and a smaller crowd checks out. A payment must never be taken twice, and the day must survive the card processor having a bad hour.
- [One-time code by text](https://systemdesigner.io/p/otp-sms-delivery/): Easy. Apps ask you to send a six-digit code to a phone. The code must arrive in seconds, a person must never get it twice, and nobody may use your system to spam a number. Texts go through a carrier partner with a hard speed limit and a real price per message.
- [Voice and video call setup](https://systemdesigner.io/p/call-routing/): Medium. People tap a name and expect the other phone to ring in a second or two. Your job is the setup: find where the person is, ring their devices and connect the two sides. Everyone calls at the same moments, like evenings and holidays.
- [Bulk text campaigns](https://systemdesigner.io/p/bulk-sms-campaigns/): Hard. Businesses send a coupon or an alert to hundreds of thousands of phones at once. Carriers accept texts only at a fixed speed, every text costs real money, and a person who replied STOP must never be texted again. Delivery receipts come back by the thousand and must be counted.
- [Status page](https://systemdesigner.io/p/status-page/): Easy. When a big service has a problem, millions of people open its status page to see what is happening. The page must stay up exactly when everything else is down, and it must not share a home with the thing it reports on. A few staff update it by hand.
- [CI/CD build system](https://systemdesigner.io/p/ci-cd-pipeline/): Medium. Every time a developer saves code to the shared repository, you build and test it. Thousands of developers do this all day, and release day brings a rush. Builds must start quickly, but idle build machines cost real money.
- [Feature flag service](https://systemdesigner.io/p/feature-flag-service/): Medium. Companies turn features on and off for groups of users without redeploying. Millions of apps ask "is this on for me?", and the answer must be instant. A wrong flag value can take down an entire customer, so changes must roll out safely and be reversible in seconds.
- [Clickstream analytics](https://systemdesigner.io/p/clickstream-analytics/): Medium. Every tap and page view on a busy site sends a tiny event to you. Hundreds of millions pile up each day. Analysts open dashboards to ask what happened this hour. Never drop an event, and keep the storage bill under control as the pile grows.
- [Metrics platform](https://systemdesigner.io/p/observability-platform/): Hard. Thousands of services send a stream of measurements: CPU, errors, latency. You store them, draw the dashboards and fire the alerts. The platform watching everyone else must never go down first, and one customer creating millions of new series can ruin the bill.
- [Logs platform](https://systemdesigner.io/p/logs-platform/): Hard. Build a shared log service for 2,000 teams. Collectors send compressed chunks, and on-call engineers find logs by tenant, service and time before filtering their words. A wide search or a runaway label must not stop other teams from investigating an outage.
- [Tracing platform](https://systemdesigner.io/p/tracing-platform/): Hard. Store distributed traces for 500 teams and make an exemplar link open the useful trace during an incident. Decide what to sample before storage, handle late spans, and keep query traffic from overwhelming ingestion. Keeping all errors is a policy goal with a failure boundary, not a magic property of sampling.
- [Metrics for many customers](https://systemdesigner.io/p/tenant-metrics/): Hard. Build one metrics platform for 5,000 customers. A tenant can create millions of series or run a costly month-long query by mistake. Your design must preserve useful ingestion and query service for the other tenants, and show the offending customer a clear limit rather than an unexplained gap.

## Lessons

- [Your first system](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/intro/): Start. Build a tiny app in three minutes and keep it standing through a rush of visitors.
- [What a request is, and p50 versus p99](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/requests-and-latency/): Start. A request is one question and one answer. Averages hide the slow ones that people remember.
- [Numbers you can do in your head](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/back-of-envelope/): Start. Turn monthly users into requests per second and servers needed, with a pencil.
- [Spreading load](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/load-balancing/): Scale the front. A load balancer hands each request to a free server so none is overwhelmed.
- [Remembering answers](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/caching/): Scale the front. A cache keeps recent answers in memory so the database is asked less.
- [Copies near users](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/cdn/): Scale the front. A CDN keeps copies of files and pages close to people, so your servers see far fewer requests.
- [Adding servers, and why it is late](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/autoscaling/): Scale the front. Autoscaling adds servers when busy, but new servers take minutes to start.
- [Copies are a little behind](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/replication-lag/): Scale the data. Read copies share the load, but they trail the original by a moment.
- [Splitting data](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/sharding/): Scale the data. When one database cannot take the writes, split the data across several.
- [When one item is popular](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/hot-keys/): Scale the data. Sharding spreads keys, not popularity. One star item can still overload one shard.
- [Search is a copy](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/search-indexing/): Scale the data. A search index is a second copy of your data, shaped for finding words fast.
- [Hot, warm, cold and archive](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/storage-tiers/): Scale the data. Old data is rarely read, so keep it somewhere cheaper and slower.
- [Waiting instead of breaking](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/queues-backpressure/): Work later. A queue lets a burst wait in line instead of crashing the thing behind it.
- [One post, millions of feeds](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/fanout/): Work later. A post by a celebrity must reach millions of feeds; do it in the background.
- [Live sockets and presence](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/realtime-connections/): Work later. Chat and live scores keep a connection open; that changes how you count capacity.
- [Which copy is the truth](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/consistency/): Stay correct. With several copies, you choose between always-latest and always-fast.
- [Exactly once, on purpose](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/idempotency-retries/): Stay correct. Retries are normal, so every action must be safe to repeat.
- [Saying "slow down" politely](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/rate-limiting/): Stay up. A limit per client stops one noisy caller or a flood from taking everyone down.
- [Timeouts and failing fast](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/circuit-breakers/): Stay up. When a dependency is slow, give up early so your servers do not pile up waiting.
- [Surviving a region](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/multi-region/): Stay up. A whole region can go dark. Run in two, and send people to the one that is up.
- [Seeing problems early](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/observability/): Stay up. You cannot fix what you cannot see: metrics, alerts and a way back.
- [Where the money goes](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/cost/): Business. Every box has a monthly price. Good design meets the goal without waste.
- [Proof built in](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/security-compliance/): Business. Auditors want proof: who did what, who can see what, and that data is protected.
- [GPUs, tokens and fallbacks](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/ai-serving/): Business. Serving AI answers is slow and expensive, so cache, limit, and have a fallback.
- [Consistent hashing and moving data](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/consistent-hashing/): Go deeper. Adding one machine can mean moving a little data or nearly all of it.
- [Copies and quorums](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/copies-quorums/): Go deeper. Copies tolerate failures when placement, acknowledgements and repair match the promise.
- [Agreeing on one leader](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/leader-consensus/): Go deeper. A leader needs a safe election and a way to stop old owners from acting.
- [What consistent really means](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/consistency-models/): Go deeper. Choose the guarantee for each operation and name what a partition changes.
- [Inside a storage engine](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/storage-engine/): Go deeper. The path from a write to disk decides memory, I/O and cost.
- [Work across services](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/work-across-services/): Go deeper. Make each step durable and show the user what is still pending.
- [Ordering and time](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/ordering-time/): Go deeper. A timestamp can sort events without proving which event caused another.
- [Syncing across devices](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/device-sync/): Go deeper. Offline edits need durable local intent, a cursor and a plan for old devices.
- [Privacy by design](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/privacy-design/): Go deeper. The safest data to protect is data the service never receives.
- [How metrics systems work](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/metrics-systems/): Go deeper. Series count, replication and query work decide the size of a metrics platform.
- [Logs and traces](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/logs-traces/): Go deeper. Keep enough evidence to explain failures without indexing or retaining everything.
- [SLOs and error budgets](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/slos-error-budgets/): Go deeper. Turn a user promise into a budget and an actionable alert.
- [Many customers on one system](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/multi-tenancy/): Go deeper. Fairness and failure boundaries matter as much as total capacity.
- [How to lead a design interview](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/lead-interview/): Lead the design. Use the hour to make decisions, test assumptions and invite useful disagreement.
- [The simplest thing that works](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/simplest-design/): Lead the design. Include people, failure recovery and future triggers in the cost of a design.
- [Changing a running system](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/running-migrations/): Lead the design. A safe migration preserves compatibility through the whole rollback window.
- [Designs that other teams must live with](https://systemdesigner.io/learn/team-boundaries/): Lead the design. A boundary is a contract and an operating responsibility, not just a box.
